summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with left lower extremity pain and hematochezia. She was found to have a supratherapeutic INR of 7.8 due to warfarin and dietary changes, leading to a spontaneous left calf hematoma and bleeding from internal hemorrhoids. She underwent incision and drainage of the hematoma, with cultures negative for infection. Warfarin was discontinued and vitamin K administered, normalizing coagulation. Anemia from acute blood loss resolved with transfusion. Her elevated tacrolimus and hypertension contributed to encephalopathy, which improved with dose adjustment and blood pressure control. Acute kidney injury and metabolic acidosis resolved. She was discharged home with home health services, stable on revised medications including amlodipine and reduced tacrolimus, with follow-up planned for surgery, nephrology, and GI.
